summary:
## Idea
A mutable disjoint-set forest with iterative path compression; the public representative is the smallest member. partition evaluates a caller conflict predicate over pairs and merges connected groups.

## Complexity
Forest union/find uses near-constant amortized inverse-Ackermann work with O(n) storage. partition additionally evaluates O(n²) pairs; it is not a linear conflict scan.

## Use when
Accumulate equivalences or group items by transitive conflict connectivity.

## Avoid when
Edges must be removed online, or directed cycles rather than equivalence components are needed.

## Pitfalls
Only indices in 0..n-1 are valid. Representative identity is a contract, not the internal tree root. A conflict component need not be a clique.

## F# usage
Package: FS.GG.Algorithms; cited source API (resolve your actual package pin).
`FS.GG.Algorithms.Graph.UnionFind.union: int -> int -> UnionFind -> bool`

```fsharp
open FS.GG.Algorithms.Graph
let groups = UnionFind.create 4
let changed = UnionFind.union 1 3 groups
let same = UnionFind.connected 1 3 groups
```

## Tests
UnionFindTests: BFS component oracle, invalid/empty cases and 100000 chained unions.

## Bench
The cited archived 0.2.0 baseline contains graph/union-find/random-unions. Read its source commit, host/date/toolchain, sizes, work counts, runtime-specific median/p95 and spread. These are GitHub-hosted runner-class comparisons, not quiet-host absolute performance; this later source revision is not itself remeasured.
